Ecological Report

Elham Ebrahimi

Source: vignettes/articles/ecological-report.Rmd
ecological-report.Rmd

Purpose of the Ecological Report

The Ecological Report is the main interpretive output of camtrapReport. It brings processed camera-trap data together into a clear, scientific-style report with narrative text, tables, figures, and maps. The report summarises key information on study context, sampling effort, species detections, activity patterns, spatial patterns, and ecological trends. It provides a reproducible and modular workflow that automates much of the reporting process, helping researchers, conservation practitioners, and camera-trap users analyse, interpret, and communicate camera-trap data efficiently for conservation planning and decision-making.

Figure 1. Workflow for generating an Ecological Report from camera-trap data using camtrapReport.

Figure 1 summarises the main workflow for generating an Ecological Report with camtrapReport. Camera-trap data are first loaded with camData(), creating an object that supports data preprocessing, manipulation, analysis, summarisation, and visualisation. This processed object is then passed to the report() function, which generates a complete HTML Ecological Report.

library(camtrapReport)

# Copy the bundled example dataset to a writable temporary directory
example_root <- tempfile("camtrapReport-example-")
dir.create(example_root, recursive = TRUE)

example_source <- system.file(
  "external",
  "dataset",
  package = "camtrapReport",
  mustWork = TRUE
)

copied <- file.copy(
  from = example_source,
  to = example_root,
  recursive = TRUE,
  copy.mode = FALSE
)

habitat <- utils::read.csv(
  system.file(
    "external",
    "habitat",
    "habitat.csv",
    package = "camtrapReport",
    mustWork = TRUE
  )
)

study_area <- system.file(
  "external",
  "study_area",
  "study_area.shp",
  package = "camtrapReport",
  mustWork = TRUE
)

stopifnot(
  isTRUE(copied),
  dir.exists(file.path(example_root, "dataset")),
  file.exists(study_area)
)

# Load the example camera-trap data and optional spatial inputs
cm <- camData(
  data = file.path(example_root, "dataset"),
  habitat = habitat,
  study_area = study_area,
  update = TRUE
)

# Generate the bundled standard Ecological Report
# Review and install optional module requirements before the full report.
report(
  cm,
  profile = "default",
  filename = file.path(example_root, "ecological-report.html"),
  view = TRUE
)

report() invisibly returns the path to the generated HTML file. By default, report.html and the intermediate report.Rmd file are written beside the writable input dataset. A specific file stem or a path inside an existing output directory can be supplied through filename:

# In a project script, check that here::here() identifies your intended root.
output_dir <- here::here("reports", "camtrapReport-ecological")
dir.create(
  output_dir,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

report_file <- report(
  cm,
  filename = file.path(output_dir, "ecological_report_2026"),
  view = FALSE
)

The resolved output and .Rmd paths are displayed before rendering. Existing files are protected by default: use a new stem for a retained report, or pass overwrite = TRUE only when you intend to replace them. A bare filename uses the object’s existing dataset directory; a missing or invalid directory raises an error, never a silent fallback to the working directory. The GUI previews the destination and leaves overwrite consent unchecked. Its initial directory uses the optional here package’s project root, or the dataset directory when here is unavailable. The core report functions do not use here.

The README quick start deliberately selects only the introduction, so it can run without the optional analysis packages. The full default and EOW profiles differ: EOW selects customised narrative and analyses and fits REM parameters separately by year; the standard profile uses pooled parameters. The report galleries below are illustrations from different datasets and configurations, rather than exact expected output from the small bundled example. Inspect a named selection with section_names(object = cm, profile = "default") or "EOW".

With test = TRUE, modules are tested and failing modules are excluded. Consequently, successful rendering can still produce an incomplete report. Read the module-test messages and resolve missing packages or inputs before treating a shortened report as a final analysis. view = TRUE requests a viewer after rendering; use view = FALSE to retain and inspect the output path if the local viewer causes problems.

Customising the Ecological Report

After the camera-trap data have been loaded with camData(), the resulting camReport object can be customised before generating the final Ecological Report. Users can adjust the report metadata, select the focal species group, define the monitoring period, apply filters, and control which report modules are included. These options allow the report to be tailored to different monitoring projects, study designs, and research aims.

Viewing and changing metadata

The contents of the camReport object are extracted or inferred from the main camera-trap dataset. These metadata can be viewed and modified using the info() function.

Use info(cm) to see all available metadata fields. Specific fields, such as the report title, subtitle, authors, institute, site name, or logo path, can also be retrieved individually. If needed, these fields can be updated before generating the final report using the following steps:

# View all available metadata fields
info(cm)

# Retrieve specific metadata fields
info(cm, name = "title")
info(cm, name = "subtitle")
info(cm, name = "authors")
info(cm, name = "institute")
info(cm, name = "siteName")
info(cm, name = "logoPath")

# Update metadata fields
info(cm, name = "title") <- "Camera-Trap Monitoring Report: Hoge Veluwe National Park, the Netherlands"
info(cm, name = "subtitle") <- "Ecological insights from long-term camera-trap data"
info(cm, name = "authors") <- c("Elham Ebrahimi", "Patrick Jansen")
info(cm, name = "institute") <- "Utrecht University, the Netherlands"
info(cm, name = "siteName") <- "Hoge Veluwe National Park"

# Optional: add an institute or project logo
info(cm, name = "logoPath") <- "path_to_logo/UU_logo.png"

# Check the updated metadata
info(cm)

Adjusting the focus group

The Ecological Report can be generated for a selected group of species, referred to as the focus_group. This allows users to focus the report on a particular taxonomic or ecological group, such as large_mammals, wild_animals, birds, amphibians, domestic, human_observation, or a custom-defined group.

Users can also define a new group by assigning records based on one or more fields, including scientificName, class, order, and observationType.

# Check the current focus group
cm$setting$focus_groups

# View available group definitions
names(cm$group_definition)

# Change the focus group
cm$set_focus_group(x = "birds")

# Re-run setup after changing the focus group
cm$setup()

# Inspect the rules used to define existing groups
cm$get_group("large_mammals")
cm$get_group("wild_animals")
cm$get_group("birds")
cm$get_group("amphibians")

A custom focus group can also be created when users want to focus on a specific set of species or records. Before defining a new group, it is useful to check the species table to see which species are available in the dataset.

# Check the list of species available in the dataset
cm$data_status$Species$Table

# Add a new custom group
cm$add_group(
  name = "target_species",
  x = list(
    scientificName = c(
      "Vulpes vulpes",
      "Capreolus capreolus",
      "Sus scrofa"
    )
  )
)

# Use the new group as the focus group
cm$set_focus_group(x = "target_species")

# Re-run setup after changing group definitions and focus group
cm$setup()

# Check the updated focus group
cm$setting$focus_groups

Selecting years and adjusting filters

Reports can be generated for all available years in the dataset or for a selected monitoring period. This is useful when users want to focus on a specific time window, such as a single monitoring year or a multi-year period. The count filter can also be adjusted to control the minimum number of observations required for a species to be included in the report.

# Check which years are available in the dataset
cm$extractYears()

# Select a specific monitoring period
cm$years <- 2023:2024

# Re-run setup after changing the selected years
cm$setup()

# Check the current count filter
cm$filterCount

# Change the minimum number of observations required
cm$filterCount <- 10

# Generate the report using the selected years and filter settings
report(
  cm,
  filename = file.path(output_dir, "ecological-report-selected-years.html"),
  view = TRUE
)

Selecting which sections are included

Users can also control which sections are included in the final report. This is useful when a shorter report is needed, or when some analyses are not relevant for a particular dataset.

# View the sections currently available
listReportSections(cm)

# Show the whole module pool (including alternative EOW modules)
section_names()

# Inspect the standard profile, excluding one section
section_names(profile = "default", exclude = "introduction")

# Exclude multiple sections
section_names(
  profile = "default",
  exclude = c("acknowledgements", "appendix")
)

# Keep only selected sections
section_names(
  profile = "default",
  keep = c("introduction", "methods", "study_area")
)

# Example: include all sections except richness and co-occurrence
selected_sections <- section_names(
  profile = "default",
  exclude = c("richness", "co_occurrence")
)

# Check the selected section names
selected_sections

# Save the selection separately so the standard profile is unchanged
selected_profile <- reportProfile(
  name = "selected",
  report = selected_sections
)
add_profile(cm, selected_profile)

# Generate the customised report
report(
  cm,
  profile = "selected",
  filename = file.path(output_dir, "ecological-report-selected.html"),
  view = TRUE
)

# Generate the standard selection again when needed
report(
  cm,
  profile = "default",
  filename = file.path(output_dir, "ecological-report-default.html")
)

The full module pool can include alternatives with the same displayed role, such as appendix and appendix_eow. Select one profile or a deliberate subset rather than attaching the whole pool, which would include both alternatives.

Reusing a report profile

A report profile records an ordered module selection while leaving the complete module pool unchanged. This is useful when the same package installation must produce different report types.

# List profiles registered in the object
profile_names(cm)

# Inspect and render a profile
section_names(object = cm, profile = "EOW")
report(
  cm,
  profile = "EOW",
  filename = file.path(output_dir, "EOW-ecological-report.html"),
  view = TRUE
)

# A PDF filename selects static PDF output
report(
  cm,
  profile = "EOW",
  filename = file.path(output_dir, "EOW-ecological-report-pdf.pdf")
)

PDF output requires the optional pagedown package and Chrome or Edge. It is created by printing the HTML report so that existing HTML-oriented modules do not need a second implementation. Interactive maps and controls are static in the PDF.

For a complete example of defining, editing, importing, and exporting a reusable selection, see the Report profiles guide.

Report progress and slow rendering

Apart from the resolved destination notice, HTML and PDF rendering is quiet by default. Enable optional console diagnostics when investigating slow rendering:

options(camtrapReport.progress = TRUE)
# Run report() or status(), then restore quiet rendering:
options(camtrapReport.progress = FALSE)

When enabled, these messages identify construction, each module/chunk, knitr completion, HTML/Pandoc rendering, PDF conversion, and output opening. Completion lines show elapsed time and CPU time in the current R process. A high R CPU time can indicate computation; a low R CPU time does not identify a specific cause, because child processes, disk access, and network waits are not measured separately. These messages do not change calculations or appear in the report. Quiet mode does not suppress warnings, errors or notices about omitted content.

If a run seems stalled, record the last started chunk and compare the same object and selection using distinct output filenames:

report(
  cm, profile = "EOW",
  filename = file.path(output_dir, "EOW-timing.html"), view = FALSE
)
report(
  cm, profile = "EOW",
  filename = file.path(output_dir, "EOW-timing-pdf.pdf"), view = FALSE
)

Run cold and same-object warm comparisons separately: successfully fitted REM models can be reused from the object. The annual EOW analysis performs species-by-year work; its repetitions and methods have not been reduced for rendering speed. A previous run ending at Rendering R Markdown report ... without a generated-file message was still in knitr/HTML rendering, before PDF conversion or view = TRUE opening.

Open an already completed file with utils::browseURL(report_file) to isolate viewer overhead. PDF printing has a 60-second timeout after browser startup; this is not a timeout on analytical computations. An error preserves the original failure rather than silently omitting analyses. Do not use test = TRUE as a performance workaround: its diagnostic recovery can exclude failed sections. After updating the package, restart R and reload the source data with update = TRUE before comparing versions.

Map backgrounds and offline use

New report objects use the shared online fallback helper. An explicit offline setting, including one stored in an older object, is never overwritten:

cm$setting$map_basemap <- "openstreetmap"
# For sensitive, disconnected or archived reports, disable all tile requests:
cm$setting$map_basemap <- "offline"

For noncommercial research reports, the automatic order is OpenStreetMap Standard → OpenStreetMap Germany → OpenTopoMap → neutral grid. It works without an additional eligibility setting. Free access is subject to each operator’s usage conditions; it is not unrestricted service capacity or a guarantee that geographic tiles will always load.

Standard requires an actual HTTP Referer for web pages. A local file:// report cannot send one and therefore starts with Germany rather than spoofing a header. Serve the report over HTTP(S), including a local HTTP server, to attempt Standard first. Tile requests reveal the viewed area to the provider; use offline mode for sensitive locations. France/HOT and Esri World Street Map are not part of the default chain: noncommercial research alone does not establish compliance with their public-site or licensing conditions.

Fallback runs in the browser even after R exits, using actual tileload and tileerror events. One isolated error does not switch a working provider. At least three unavailable tiles and 75% failed coverage trigger failover once the current viewport settles. An eight-second deadline also advances a stalled provider if no useful tiles arrive or that failure threshold is reached; otherwise useful imagery is retained and outstanding requests are cancelled. Only one online background is active, and each provider is attempted at most once per failure cascade. If all fail, the neutral grid remains without stopping the report. Hidden/nested tabs resize when activated and do not prefetch unseen tiles. Markers, polygons, rasters, legends, extent, zoom and controls are retained. During printing, unfinished tiles use the neutral background; completed imagery can remain. Backgrounds paused only for printing resume afterwards; exhausted providers and explicit offline mode do not restart. The grid is not a downloaded tile archive.

Read the OSMF tile policy and OpenTopoMap usage conditions. Both require visible attribution and prohibit excessive or bulk downloading; neither provides an uptime guarantee. The German service conditions restrict embedding to noncommercial use, with a small-use exception. The package retains visible credits for the active provider: OpenStreetMap contributors for Standard/Germany, or OpenStreetMap/SRTM/OpenTopoMap with the latter’s CC-BY-SA licence. Retain these credits when exporting maps. A disconnected or blocked network can make all online backgrounds unavailable. The neutral grid keeps the ecological overlays readable in that case, but is not a geographic basemap.

Existing explicit "cartodb" and "esri" settings remain for compatibility, with a neutral error fallback. They remain subject to the operators’ terms. Esri use requires applicable service licensing; anonymous endpoint access is not itself a licence. CARTO’s current raster service requires an API key; the legacy keyless mode is not a promise of a licensed or unwatermarked service. The package does not add a credential-management API in this revision. Prefer offline mode for private data, archives or disconnected viewing.

A generated report summarises the implemented checks and selected analyses. It does not establish that the survey design is suitable for a particular ecological question or that the data satisfy all assumptions of the selected methods. Outputs should be interpreted in relation to sampling effort, detectability, season, habitat, and method-specific assumptions.

Together, these options allow users to generate Ecological Reports that are reproducible, flexible, and tailored to the aims of each camera-trap monitoring project.
